The fxctl tool

This lesson gets you to run fx from the shell with fxctl and read what it prints. fxctl is a command-line wrapper around fx: one command passes a number to fx and prints what fx returns. You will complete the command yourself.

fxctl is a command-line wrapper around fx: fxctl run takes one number, calls fx on it and prints the result.

What it prints is what fx returns. [1]

Run fx on 7 through fxctl:

$ fxctl run 7
42

The one line of output is fx(7), from the experiment [3].

Fill in the missing word, then check the output you expect.

$ fxctl ____ 7
42

Run this unaided. You should see 18 printed.

fxctl run 3
